Header:
Date: 2025-02-11

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be noisy):
- Goal: scope a 4-week POC to validate model quality for ZenHealth patient triage and note generation.
- Deliverables: golden prompts, eval harness, benchmark run (latency + hallucination), scoring rubric.
- Success criteria drafted: hallucination rate <5% on critical fields, P95 latency <350ms for synchronous API, structured output match >= 92% exact/field-level, human-validated accept rate >90% on sampled outputs.

Topics (auto): success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks, timelines, quality eval plan (golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination checks, scoring approach)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan Patel (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We can do quick intros — I'll be Jordan, I'm the AE on this. Alex is our SE who will own the eval harness and performance questions.
[00:10] Maria Lopez (ZenHealth): Hi all, Maria here. We're hoping to run a pilot to see if Redwood can meet our safety and accuracy bar for triage and note generation.
[00:18] Devon Carter (ZenHealth): Devon — platform eng. We'll also care a lot about deployment model. On-prem vs VPC — we have strict data residency.
[00:24] Alex Ng (Redwood): Quick note: we typically run the POC on Redwood Dedicated to simplify latency tests, but we can emulate private if needed. We'll capture logs and can run the same harness across hosted/dedicated/private.
[00:33] Anika Bose (ZenHealth): Important — we need structured outputs for our EHR ingestion. So format must be exact (date formats, ICD codes, fields).
[00:40] Jordan Patel (Redwood): Great, that aligns. For today's goal: agree success criteria and the eval plan — golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination/format checks, scoring approach, and timeline.

[00:55] Alex Ng (Redwood): I'll start with workload sizing. Maria, can you confirm expected volume? You mentioned roughly 150k user interactions per month and peak 8 qps?
[01:05] Maria Lopez (ZenHealth): That's right, ballpark. Some days are 10k interactions, but for POC we want a scaled-down sim: ~10k total over test window.
[01:12] Devon Carter (ZenHealth): Peak concurrent in production could be up to 25 qps for short bursts. For the POC we don't expect more than 4-8 qps, but we want headroom.
[01:20] Alex Ng (Redwood): OK, we'll size the dedicated pod to emulate 25 qps headroom in load tests. For latency expectations, what's your SLO?
[01:27] Anika Bose (ZenHealth): For synchronous triage API, ideally P95 <200ms but we understand that might be optimistic for long responses. P95 <350ms would be acceptable.
[01:35] Jordan Patel (Redwood): Noted. We'll report both cold and steady-state P95. Our default config uses KV cache and batching — that drives cost/latency tradeoffs.

[01:50] Maria Lopez (ZenHealth): On quality, we care about hallucinations on key fields (diagnosis, medication). Even a single wrong medication is high risk. How do you measure hallucination?
[01:58] Alex Ng (Redwood): Good question. For the POC we propose a hybrid eval: automated checks + human review. Automated checks include schema validation (format/fields), entity matching against a whitelist (e.g., ICD10 codes), and paraphrase detection to flag unexpected tokens. Then sample outputs go to human annotators for hallucination labeling.
[02:12] Devon Carter (ZenHealth): Entity matching sounds good. What about hallucination thresholds?
[02:18] Jordan Patel (Redwood): Proposed threshold: less than 5% hallucination on critical fields for the pilot to be considered successful. Critical fields = medication list, primary diagnosis, allergy statements. Non-critical free-text can be more lenient.

[02:32] Maria Lopez (ZenHealth): 5% might still be high for safety — can we set gating: automated blocking on medication mismatches (zero tolerance) and a 2% allowed on diagnosis?
[02:41] Alex Ng (Redwood): We can do gating rules: block any output that fails strict medication whitelist check. For scoring, we'll have per-field thresholds and an overall composite score.

[02:55] Anika Bose (ZenHealth): For structured outputs, we'll need exact-match per field. Is Redwood doing token-level diff or semantic match?
[03:02] Samir Rao (Redwood Product): We'll use a layered approach: exact-match for fields with enumerated values (dates, codes), normalized string compare for freeform but structured fields (strip punctuation/case), and BLEU/ROUGE or embedding similarity for longer narrative sections. But for EHR ingestion, exact-match pass/fail is the most important.

[03:20] Jordan Patel (Redwood): About golden prompts — we suggest ZenHealth provide 50 golden prompts covering happy path and edge cases, plus Redwood will add another 50 variants. The golden prompts will include expected outputs and scoring labels.
[03:33] Maria Lopez (ZenHealth): We can do that. We'll craft prompts that mirror clinician notes and patient messages. We'll also annotate expected ICD10 codes where applicable.

[03:45] Alex Ng (Redwood): Regression tests: we'll maintain a suite that runs on each model/quantization change. Tests: 1) schema validation, 2) hallucination detection checks, 3) formatting checks (date/units), 4) end-to-end EHR ingestion simulation. Failures will be flagged and the model rolled back or routed to a different variant per rollout policy.

[04:10] Devon Carter (ZenHealth): Can you explain how rollback/variant routing works? If a new model deploys and regression fails, we want automated fallback.
[04:17] Alex Ng (Redwood): Yes — Redwood rollouts can define canary thresholds. If regression suite fails beyond X% we automatically route traffic to previous stable variant. For the POC we can capture that, but full automation requires Dedicated or Private deployment. We can demo manual fallback for hosted.

[04:35] Anika Bose (ZenHealth): Scoring approach — we need a single dashboard metric for executive stakeholders. What do you propose?
[04:41] Samir Rao (Redwood): Composite quality score computed as weighted sum: 40% critical-field exact-match, 25% hallucination-free rate, 20% format/schema pass rate, 15% human accept rate on sampled outputs. We'll produce per-run and cumulative scores and show trend lines. Weighting is configurable.

[04:58] Maria Lopez (ZenHealth): That seems reasonable. Can weights be tuned post-POC?
[05:02] Jordan Patel (Redwood): Absolutely — we'll give you a starting config and a small UI to tweak weights.

[05:12] Speaker 1 (customer, unclear): [mumble] — legal wants to know about logging and PHI retention.
[05:17] Roger Lim (ZenHealth - Legal): Quick point: PHI retention outside our VPC is a show-stopper. We need KMS integration and audit logs. For the POC, masked data is possible but ultimately we need private deployment.
[05:29] Priya Menon (Redwood CSM): We have an on-prem/private option. For the POC we can run with de-identified data, and then run an on-prem pilot if the results meet quality. We'll include KMS/HSM options in the security doc.

[05:46] Jordan Patel (Redwood): Timeline proposal: week 0 (this week) — finalize success criteria and golden prompt list. Week 1 — Redwood builds eval harness and ingest pipeline; customer shares sample data. Week 2 — dry-run and tuning. Week 3 — full benchmark runs (latency + quality). Week 4 — results review and decision on next steps. So roughly 4 weeks total.
[06:03] Maria Lopez (ZenHealth): That fits our internal timeline. We want final decision by mid-March.

[06:10] Alex Ng (Redwood): On benchmarks we'll run two axes: performance (latency/QPS/cost) and quality (the scoring suite). For perf: cold start, steady-state, burst tests. We'll report P50/P95/P99 and cost per 1k tokens. For quality: pass rates on golden prompts, hallucination %, exact-match fields.

[06:27] Devon Carter (ZenHealth): Cost reporting please — we need token-level and per-transaction cost for our forecasting.
[06:31] Jordan Patel (Redwood): We'll include token breakdown and per-route cost estimates in the pilot pricing sheet.

[06:40] Maria Lopez (ZenHealth): Regarding hallucination detection, do you run specialized classifiers or rely on rule-based checks?
[06:46] Alex Ng (Redwood): We'll combine both: rule-based whitelist/blacklist for critical fields + a lightweight hallucination classifier trained on prompt-output pairs to flag unlikely entities. Ultimately human review for flagged cases.

[06:58] Anika Bose (ZenHealth): For regression test automation, will tests run nightly?
[07:02] Samir Rao (Redwood): For POC we'll run scheduled test runs tied to model changes and nightly if requested. Each run will produce a report and we can export CSV for audit.

[07:12] Maria Lopez (ZenHealth): We also want sample-level evidence for audits — a sample of 50 outputs with annotations.
[07:17] Jordan Patel (Redwood): We will provide that. Redwood's console will show per-sample diffs and annotator comments.

[07:26] Devon Carter (ZenHealth): Any special handling for private deployment metrics?
[07:29] Priya Menon (Redwood): If you go Private, metrics can be pushed to your internal telemetry; we can mirror logs to your SIEM. For POC we'll stream anonymized metrics.

[07:40] Maria Lopez (ZenHealth): Can you share an example of a golden prompt and expected output?
[07:45] Alex Ng (Redwood): Sure — example (paraphrasing): Prompt: "Patient reports shortness of breath and chest pain, 57 y/o, hx of HTN. Provide likely diagnosis, suggested ICD10, and meds to consider." Expected structured output: primary_diagnosis: I20.0, icd10_codes: ["I20.0"], meds: ["nitroglycerin"], note: <1-2 sentence summary>. We'll include normalization rules for codes and medication canonicalization.

[08:08] Maria Lopez (ZenHealth): Good. Also need hallucination/format checks for dates and units (mg vs mg/dL mixups).
[08:14] Alex Ng (Redwood): We'll add unit normalization tests.

[08:18] Jordan Patel (Redwood): On scoring thresholds, current proposal (for POC pass): composite quality score >= 92, critical-field exact-match >= 95, hallucination critical fields = 0 tolerable (block/fail), overall hallucination rate < 5. We can refine with you.

[08:36] Anika Bose (ZenHealth): Composite 92 sounds aggressive but acceptable for pilot if strict gating is in place on meds.

[08:44] Speaker 2 (mild crosstalk): [someone] — can Redwood publish the regression suite so we can run locally?
[08:48] Alex Ng (Redwood): Yes. We'll provide a dockerized runner and the test manifest; you can run it in your environment with masked data.

[08:58] Roger Lim (ZenHealth - Legal): We'll need an addendum about data handling. For now assume de-id for POC.

[09:04] Jordan Patel (Redwood): We'll send our standard POC checklist and security pack (SOC2 summary, KMS options, data flow diagrams).

[09:11] Maria Lopez (ZenHealth): One more — human review process: who will label hallucinations? Internal team or Redwood annotators?
[09:18] Alex Ng (Redwood): Both options. For scale we can use Redwood's vetted annotators with healthcare expertise under an NDA; alternatively you can run labeling in-house. For the POC we recommend Redwood does initial labeling and we share raw annotations.

[09:32] Anika Bose (ZenHealth): If Redwood's annotators label, we need to see inter-annotator agreement stats.
[09:36] Samir Rao (Redwood): We'll include Cohen's kappa and raw agreement percentages in the annotation report.

[09:45] Jordan Patel (Redwood): To recap next steps: Jordan to share pilot pricing and POC checklist; Alex to deliver eval harness + docker runner and initial golden prompts; Maria to share sample dataset and 50 golden prompts; schedule benchmark week of 2/24.

[09:58] Maria Lopez (ZenHealth): Sounds good. Any blockers from legal?
[10:02] Roger Lim (ZenHealth - Legal): Not for de-id data. For full pilot with PHI we'll need the private deployment contract terms.

[10:10] Jordan Patel (Redwood): Understood. We'll prepare a path to private pilot if POC passes.

[10:16] Alex Ng (Redwood): One last technical note: we recommend running both quantized and FP16 variants to compare cost/quality tradeoff. We'll include configs.
[10:24] Devon Carter (ZenHealth): Good. Please include expected accuracy delta in the report.

[10:30] Jordan Patel (Redwood): OK, wrapping up. Thanks everyone — we'll circulate minutes and agreed action items.

[10:40] Meeting end.

Notes on evaluation specifics (post-meeting edit by Redwood SE):
- Golden prompts: 100 total (50 from ZenHealth, 50 from Redwood). Each golden prompt tagged with expected output schema, critical fields, and labeling instructions.
- Regression suite: automated runner executes against current model artifact. Outputs: per-test pass/fail, per-field exact-match, hallucination flags, normalized score. Reports exported as CSV/JSON (we'll also provide PDF summary).
- Hallucination/format checks: 1) Schema validator for required fields; 2) ICD10 whitelist matching (exact); 3) medication canonicalization using RxNorm map (best-effort) and block if unknown med suggested; 4) date/unit normalization; 5) hallucination classifier run to flag free-text anomalies.
- Scoring approach: compute per-sample scores then average: field_exact_score (0 or 1 per critical field) aggregated; hallucination_penalty applied if classifier or human labels indicate hallucination; human_accept_rate sampled at N=200 (or all failures) with adjudication. Composite score normalized to 0-100.
- Acceptance gating: any medication mismatch triggers fail for that sample and increments regression fail count; if >2% of samples fail gating the run is considered failed.
- Benchmarks: latency (P50/P95/P99), throughput (QPS with 95th percentile under burst), cost per 1k tokens, warm/cold start deltas.
